## Authentication

Every request needs an MCPJam API key in the `A

uthorization` header:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -X POST \
 "https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/
$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/tools\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/jso

n" \
 -d '{}'
```

### Creating a key

1. Open [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)
 in
the hosted app (the card at the top of this page takes you there\n directly).\n2. Click **Create API key**, name it, and pick t
he **organization** it will act in.\n3. Copy the key (`sk_…`) immediately — **it is shown exactly once** and never\n stored by M

CPJam in retrievable form.

Keys can be revoked from the same page at any time. Revocation takes effect
immediately.

### Sco

pe

A key is bound to one MCPJam organization at creation and acts **as you,
inside that organization**. Per-request authorizat
ion still applies: a call\nonly succeeds if the key's owner can access that project and server. A key\ncan never reach projects ou

tside its organization.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Two deliberate restrictions while in preview:
>
> * **API keys cannot manage API keys
.** Requests to the key-management surface\n> with an `sk_…` bearer fail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. Create and revoke keys in\n> th

e UI.
> * **Guest sessions cannot use the API.** Sign in to create keys.

### Keep keys secret

Treat an API key like a passw

ord:

* Load it from an environment variable or secret manager — never commit it to
 source control or ship it in client-side
code.\n* Scope keys narrowly: one key per integration, named so you can tell them apart.\n* Rotate by creating a replacement key,
switching traffic, then revoking the old one.\n* If a key leaks, revoke it immediately in\n [**Settings → API keys**](https://app

.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

If you see `401 UNAUTHORIZED` with `details.reason: "ORPHANED_KEY"`, the key
is no longer bo

und to an organization and cannot be used — create a new key
from [Settings](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

## Con

ventions

**Requests.** Operations on servers are `POST` with a JSON body (most accept
an empty `{}`). **Reads** — the catalog

listings and eval-run polling — are
`GET` and take their options (`cursor`, `limit`, filters) as query
parameters.

**Response

s.** Three envelope shapes, used consistently:

| Kind | Shape |
| - | - |
| Single resource | The resource object directly |\
n| Collection | `{ \"items\": [...], \"nextCursor\": \"...\" }` — `nextCursor` omitted on the last page |\n| Error | `{ \"code\":
\"...\", \"message\": \"...\", \"details\": {...} }` with a matching HTTP status |\n\n**Pagination.** Collections are cursor-based
. Pass the previous response's\n`nextCursor` as `cursor` in the next request (body field on `POST` lists,\nquery parameter on `GET
` lists). Cursors are opaque — don't parse them.\n\n**Authoring vs running suites.** `POST /eval-suites` creates a runnable suite\
n(the suite plus its test cases) **synchronously** and responds `201` with the\n`suiteId`, WITHOUT running anything — author once,
run later. `POST /eval-runs`\nis the async counterpart: it validates and creates a run synchronously, then\ndetaches execution an
d responds `202` with a `runId`. Poll\n`GET /eval-runs/{runId}` until `status` is `completed`, `failed`,\n`cancelled`, or `timed_o

ut`.

**IDs.** Every identifier the API takes is discoverable through the API
itself: `GET /projects` lists your projects, `GET
/projects/{projectId}/servers`\nlists each project's servers, and `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites`\nlists its eval suites.

Start from `GET /me` to confirm which account a key
acts as.

## Errors

Errors always use the canonical body `{ code, messa
ge, details? }`. The `code`\nis stable and machine-readable; `message` is human-readable and may change;\n`details` is an optional

, unstructured bag.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | Missing, invalid, revoked, or orphaned k
ey |\n| `OAUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | The **target MCP server** needs an OAuth grant — distinct from a bad key |\n| `AUTH_REQUIRED` | 4
03 | The **target MCP server** allowed the connection and asked for sign-in on this call. `details.authChallenge` carries the pars
ed challenge. Your key is fine — see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-in-challenges) |\n| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Key is valid but not allow
ed to do this — or the **target MCP server** rejected the credentials MCPJam presented (retrying with a different MCPJam key will
not help; reconnect or re-authorize the server) |\n| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | Malformed body or parameters |\n| `NOT_FOUND` | 40
4 | Unknown project, server, or resource |\n| `CONFLICT` | 409 | The resource isn't in a state that accepts this write — a stale `
expectedRevision`, a duplicate name, or an environment that can't currently be launched. Re-read and retry |\n| `FEATURE_NOT_SUPPO
RTED` | 422 | The target server doesn't support this MCP capability |\n| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests — see [Rate limi
ts](#rate-limits) |\n| `SERVER_UNREACHABLE` | 502 | Could not connect to the target MCP server |\n| `TIMEOUT` | 504 | The target M

CP server connected but didn't respond in time |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Something failed on our side |

New error codes may

be **added** over time; treat unknown codes as
non-retryable failures unless the HTTP status says otherwise.

### Sign-in chal

lenges

Some MCP servers allow the connection and ask for sign-in only on a protected
call. The API never starts a sign-in. It

reports the challenge instead:

* **HTTP 401 from the MCP server** on `tools/call`: the API answers
 `403 AUTH_REQUIRED`. `det
ails.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge:\n its `source` (`http_401`), and the `error`, `requiredScope`, and\n `resource
MetadataUrl` the server sent, when present.\n* **An `isError` result carrying `_meta[\"mcp/www_authenticate\"]`** (the\n ChatGPT
convention): the call succeeds, and the `CallToolResult` is returned\n unchanged with an additive `authChallenge` field (`source:

"tool_result_meta"`). A field the server already set under that name is never
 overwritten.

`AUTH_REQUIRED` is not `UNA
UTHORIZED`: your MCPJam key is fine, so a different\nkey will not help. Complete the OAuth flow for that server yourself, upload t
he\ntoken to one of its [accounts](#server-accounts), and call again. See\n[Mid-session sign-in](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector

/lazy-authentication.md).

## Rate limits

Each key gets **60 requests per minute** sustained, with bursts up to **10**.
Exce

eding it returns `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header (in
seconds):

```http theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
HTT

P/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 7

{ "code": "RATE_LIMITED", "message": "API key rate limit exceeded. Slow down

and retry." }
```

Honor `Retry-After`, add jittered exponential backoff, and expect these limits
to be tuned during the pre

view.

Other `429`s — the per-minute brakes and daily budgets described with the
endpoints below — carry `Retry-After` whenever
the refusal knows when it\nlifts, which is the ordinary case. Treat it as a hint that is usually there\nrather than a guarantee:

a refusal that reaches you without one still needs
your backoff, so **never** block waiting for a header that may not come.

##

Endpoints

Each endpoint is fully documented — request and response schemas, examples,
and an interactive playground — under *

*Endpoints** in the sidebar.

**Catalog** — discover the IDs everything else takes:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
|
`GET /me` | The account behind the key |\n| `GET /organizations` | The organizations the caller belongs to — where `organizationI
d` comes from. A key is bound to one organization and only ever sees that one |\n| `GET /projects` | Projects the key can access (
optionally `?organizationId=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers` | The project's saved MCP servers |\n| `GET /projects/{pro
jectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions` | A server's stored revisions, newest first: captures of its tools and server info, recorded
whenever they change (`?limit=&cursor=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}` | One rev
